```{python}
#| label: setup

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go
import plotly.io as pio
from IPython.display import HTML, display

# Design tokens, taken verbatim from the live app's stylesheet so the deck
# and the product read as one system.
PAPER = "#0e1116"   # --paper (dark)
INK   = "#f5f2ec"   # --ink   (dark)
SLATE = "#1a2028"
GAIN  = "#2f7d6e"
LOSS  = "#a8442f"
BRASS = "#c9a227"
MUTED = "#8b929c"
GRID  = "#232a33"

pio.templates["ticker"] = go.layout.Template(
    layout=dict(
        paper_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)",
        plot_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)",
        font=dict(family="Instrument Sans, ui-sans-serif, system-ui", color=INK, size=15),
        colorway=[BRASS, GAIN, LOSS, MUTED],
        xaxis=dict(gridcolor=GRID, zerolinecolor=GRID, linecolor=GRID,
                   tickfont=dict(family="IBM Plex Mono, monospace", size=13, color=MUTED)),
        yaxis=dict(gridcolor=GRID, zerolinecolor=GRID, linecolor=GRID,
                   tickfont=dict(family="IBM Plex Mono, monospace", size=13, color=MUTED)),
        # Legend sits *below* the plot: the top strip is reserved for the
        # updatemenu buttons, and the two collide if both live up there.
        legend=dict(bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)", font=dict(size=13, color=MUTED),
                    orientation="h", yanchor="top", y=-0.14, x=0),
        margin=dict(l=64, r=28, t=60, b=76),
        hoverlabel=dict(bgcolor=SLATE, bordercolor=BRASS,
                        font=dict(family="IBM Plex Mono, monospace", size=13, color=INK)),
    )
)
pio.templates.default = "ticker"

# Fixed seed. Every illustrative series in this deck is reproducible.
rng = np.random.default_rng(20260907)

CONFIG = {"displayModeBar": False, "responsive": True}

# Emit charts as plain HTML rather than via fig.show().
#
# fig.show() goes through a plotly *renderer*, and every renderer either
# fetches plotly.js from a CDN or (the "notebook" one) pulls requirejs and
# jquery from a CDN to load it — either way the deck stops working without a
# network. The library is loaded from libs/plotly.min.js in <head> instead
# (see theme/plotly-head.html), so each chart emits only its own init call.
def show(fig):
    height = fig.layout.height or 500
    html = pio.to_html(
        fig,
        include_plotlyjs=False,          # loaded once, from <head>
        full_html=False,
        config=CONFIG,
        default_width="100%",
        default_height=f"{height}px",
    )
    display(HTML(html))

def menu_style(**kw):
    """Shared styling for Plotly's updatemenus, in the deck's palette."""
    base = dict(
        type="buttons", direction="right",
        bgcolor=SLATE, bordercolor=GRID, borderwidth=1,
        font=dict(family="IBM Plex Mono, monospace", size=12, color=INK),
        pad=dict(r=6, t=6), showactive=True, active=0,
        x=0, xanchor="left", y=1.20, yanchor="top",
    )
    base.update(kw)
    return base
```

##  {#title .center}

::: {style="max-width:26em"}
[Engineering Guide · v1.0 · September 2026]{.kicker}

::: {style="font-family:'Bricolage Grotesque',sans-serif;font-weight:700;font-size:4.6em;line-height:0.95;letter-spacing:-0.04em;margin:0.1em 0 0 0"}
Ticker
:::

::: {.title-lead}
A single-machine stock dashboard: live prices streamed to the browser, a
portfolio derived from an append-only ledger, and an AI analyst that can
propose changes but **never make them**.
:::

::: {style="margin-top:1.4em;font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',monospace;font-size:0.4em;letter-spacing:0.14em;text-transform:uppercase;color:#8b929c"}
AAPL [187.42]{data-tick="187.42" style="color:#2f7d6e"} &nbsp;·&nbsp;
MSFT [418.09]{data-tick="418.09" style="color:#2f7d6e"} &nbsp;·&nbsp;
NVDA [126.55]{data-tick="126.55" style="color:#a8442f"} &nbsp;·&nbsp;
ticker-dash.fly.dev
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Fifteen minutes. The thesis: this is a small system that takes two ideas
seriously — that a ledger is the only truth, and that a model may propose but
never execute. Everything else follows from those two.
:::

## One process, on purpose

::: {.split}
::: {}
::: {.pull}
Everything below the browser runs as a single Python process on a single machine.
:::

::: {style="margin-top:0.8em;font-size:0.62em;line-height:1.55;color:#8b929c"}
That is a **deliberate constraint, not a limitation of scale.**
:::

::: {.stages style="margin-top:0.6em"}
::: {.stage}
[01]{.n}[The market feed allows **one connection per key**. [A second machine would open a second socket.]{.m}]{.t}
:::
::: {.stage}
[02]{.n}[The database is **a file on a disk that cannot be mounted twice**. [Two copies, two divergent ledgers.]{.m}]{.t}
:::
:::
:::

::: {}
[The five layers]{.kicker}

::: {style="font-size:0.5em;line-height:1.5"}
**Data** — rented feeds + SQLite<br>
[Finnhub, Twelve Data, Anthropic. Local state in one SQLite file on a Fly volume.]{.muted}

**Processing** — providers + services<br>
[Provider interface, TTL cache, price hub, FIFO lot engine, chat loop.]{.muted}

**Application** — FastAPI<br>
[14 REST routes, one WebSocket, one SSE stream, all behind a session gate.]{.muted}

**Visualisation** — React + lightweight-charts<br>
[Zustand for high-frequency prices, TanStack Query for REST.]{.muted}

**Output** — one page, one origin<br>
[The API serves the built SPA: one deploy, and no CORS.]{.muted}
:::
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
The "one origin" decision at the bottom is why there is no CORS configuration
anywhere in the codebase. It also means you cannot fetch this API from a slide
deck — I tried.
:::

::: {}
::: {.pull style="font-size:1.15em"}
The rate mismatch is the design problem.
:::

::: {style="font-size:0.5em;line-height:1.55;color:#8b929c;margin-top:0.7em"}
A liquid symbol prints **hundreds of trades a second**. A browser cannot redraw
that often.

The `PriceHub` keeps the latest price per symbol and flushes at most every
**250 ms**, so the browser receives a bounded trickle.

The store is keyed by symbol, so **one tick re-renders one row** — not the table.
:::

::: {.card style="margin-top:0.9em"}
[Invariant]{.tag}[Track A never sees the database]{.h4}

A price is not a fact worth persisting. It is overwritten, coalesced, pushed, and forgotten.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
This is the slide to slow down on. Everything gold is pushed; everything else
in the system is requested. The next slide shows what that ratio actually
looks like.
:::

## The rate mismatch {.center}

[Figure · what coalescing actually does]{.kicker}

```{python}
#| label: rate-mismatch

DURATION   = 3.0      # seconds on screen
TRADES_SEC = 300      # "hundreds per second"
N = int(DURATION * TRADES_SEC)

# A plausible intraday walk. The price is scenery; the *density* is the point.
t = np.sort(rng.uniform(0, DURATION, N))
price = 187.40 + np.cumsum(rng.normal(0, 0.006, N))

def coalesce(interval_ms):
    """PriceHub.flush(): last price per symbol, at most once per interval."""
    step = interval_ms / 1000.0
    edges = np.arange(step, DURATION + step, step)
    xs, ys = [], []
    for e in edges:
        taken = price[t <= e]
        if len(taken):
            xs.append(e)
            ys.append(taken[-1])
    return xs, ys

x250, y250 = coalesce(250)

def note(interval_ms, n_out):
    return [dict(
        x=0.02, y=0.97, xref="paper", yref="paper",
        xanchor="left", yanchor="top", showarrow=False, align="left",
        font=dict(family="IBM Plex Mono, monospace", size=17, color=INK),
        bgcolor="rgba(26,32,40,0.85)", bordercolor=BRASS, borderwidth=1,
        borderpad=9,
        text=(f"<b>{N} prints in</b>  →  <b style='color:{BRASS}'>{n_out} frames out</b>"
              f"<br><span style='font-size:13px;color:{MUTED}'>"
              f"flush every {interval_ms} ms · {N/max(n_out,1):.0f}× reduction</span>"),
    )]

fig = go.Figure()

# Every trade that arrives on the socket.
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=t, y=price, mode="markers", name=f"trade prints · {TRADES_SEC}/s",
    marker=dict(size=3.4, color=MUTED, opacity=0.5),
    hovertemplate="print<br>%{x:.3f}s · $%{y:.2f}<extra></extra>",
))

# What the browser is actually sent.
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=x250, y=y250, mode="lines+markers", name="pushed to browser",
    line=dict(color=BRASS, width=2.5, shape="hv"),
    marker=dict(size=9, color=BRASS, line=dict(color=PAPER, width=2)),
    hovertemplate="flush<br>%{x:.3f}s · $%{y:.2f}<extra></extra>",
))

buttons = []
for ms in (100, 250, 1000):
    xs, ys = coalesce(ms)
    buttons.append(dict(
        label=f"  {ms} ms  ",
        method="update",
        args=[{"x": [t, xs], "y": [price, ys]}, {"annotations": note(ms, len(xs))}],
    ))

fig.update_layout(
    height=560, autosize=True,
    annotations=note(250, len(x250)),
    xaxis=dict(title="seconds", range=[0, DURATION]),
    yaxis=dict(title="price", tickprefix="$"),
    updatemenus=[menu_style(buttons=buttons, active=1)],
    hovermode="closest",
)
show(fig)
```

[Illustrative — the coalescing ratio described in the guide, not a recording of real trades. Try the flush interval: 100 ms is smoother and four times the traffic; 1000 ms is cheap and visibly laggy. 250 ms is the shipped compromise.]{.caption}

::: {.notes}
Click the buttons. At 100 ms the gold line hugs the cloud but you have
quadrupled the frames. At 1000 ms you can see the staircase lag behind the
market. 250 ms is where it stops looking laggy and stops costing much.
:::

::: {.cols style="margin-top:0.7em;font-size:0.44em;line-height:1.5"}
::: {.fragment}
[**A · never touches SQLite.**]{.brass} Hundreds in, ≤ 4/s out. Overwritten and forgotten.
:::
::: {.fragment}
[**B · the only ordinary write path.**]{.gain} Oversell is rejected *first*, in one transaction — a refusal leaves nothing behind.
:::
::: {.fragment}
[**C · proposes.**]{.brass} The diamond is the only gate between a model proposal and a recorded trade.
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Three tracks, one set of services. They differ in what starts them and what
they are allowed to touch. Green = writes. Gold = pushed or gated.
:::

## Track B · Transactions are truth {.center}

[Figure · why no share count is stored]{.kicker}

```{python}
#| label: fifo-lots

# Three buys, then one sell of 60 shares at $205.
LOTS = [("Lot 1 · Jan 12", 40, 150.0), ("Lot 2 · Mar 04", 30, 172.0), ("Lot 3 · May 21", 30, 198.0)]
SELL_QTY, SELL_PX = 60, 205.0

# FIFO: consume oldest lots first.
remaining = SELL_QTY
sold_f, held_f, realized_f = [], [], 0.0
for _, qty, px in LOTS:
    take = min(qty, remaining)
    remaining -= take
    sold_f.append(take)
    held_f.append(qty - take)
    realized_f += take * (SELL_PX - px)

total_qty  = sum(q for _, q, _ in LOTS)
total_cost = sum(q * p for _, q, p in LOTS)
avg_px     = total_cost / total_qty
realized_a = SELL_QTY * (SELL_PX - avg_px)

labels_f = [f"{n}<br>${p:,.0f}" for n, _, p in LOTS]
labels_a = [f"Single blended position<br>${avg_px:,.2f}"]

def banner(method, realized, sub):
    colour = GAIN if realized >= 0 else LOSS
    return [dict(
        x=0.99, y=0.97, xref="paper", yref="paper",
        xanchor="right", yanchor="top", showarrow=False, align="right",
        font=dict(family="IBM Plex Mono, monospace", size=16, color=INK),
        bgcolor="rgba(26,32,40,0.85)", bordercolor=colour, borderwidth=1, borderpad=9,
        # Plotly's SVG text parser accepts <span style>, but not a style
        # attribute on <b> — one of those blanks the whole annotation.
        text=(f"{method} · realized P/L "
              f"<span style='color:{colour};font-size:21px'><b>${realized:,.0f}</b></span>"
              f"<br><span style='font-size:13px;color:{MUTED}'>{sub}</span>"),
    )]

fig = go.Figure()
fig.add_trace(go.Bar(
    x=labels_f, y=sold_f, name=f"sold @ ${SELL_PX:,.0f}",
    marker=dict(color=BRASS, line=dict(color=PAPER, width=1)),
    hovertemplate="sold %{y} shares<extra></extra>",
))
fig.add_trace(go.Bar(
    x=labels_f, y=held_f, name="still held",
    marker=dict(color=SLATE, line=dict(color="#39424e", width=1)),
    hovertemplate="held %{y} shares<extra></extra>",
))

fig.update_layout(
    height=505, autosize=True, barmode="stack", bargap=0.55,
    yaxis=dict(title="shares", range=[0, 45]),
    xaxis=dict(title=""),
    annotations=banner("FIFO", realized_f, "40 @ $150 + 20 @ $172 consumed, oldest first"),
    updatemenus=[menu_style(buttons=[
        dict(label="  FIFO lots  ", method="update",
             args=[{"x": [labels_f, labels_f], "y": [sold_f, held_f]},
                   {"annotations": banner("FIFO", realized_f,
                                          "40 @ $150 + 20 @ $172 consumed, oldest first")}]),
        dict(label="  Average cost  ", method="update",
             args=[{"x": [labels_a, labels_a], "y": [[SELL_QTY], [total_qty - SELL_QTY]]},
                   {"annotations": banner("Average cost", realized_a,
                                          "lot structure gone — and it cannot be recovered")}]),
    ])],
)
show(fig)
```

::: {.cols style="margin-top:0.3em"}
::: {}
[Illustrative lots. Same three buys, same sale — **$`{python} f"{realized_f - realized_a:,.0f}"`** apart in realized P/L.]{.caption}
:::
::: {}
[Positions, cost basis and P/L are **recomputed** from the log every time. The log is append-only; a correction is a new row.]{.caption}
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Toggle to Average cost. The bars collapse into one — and that is the whole
argument. Average cost destroys the lot structure, so the moment you sell part
of a position you can never recover the real basis. Hence: store no share count.
:::

## Track C · The model proposes {.center}

::: {.split}
::: {}
::: {.pull style="font-size:1.2em"}
It can propose portfolio changes but cannot make them. Nothing is written until you click Confirm.
:::

::: {style="font-size:0.44em;line-height:1.5;color:#8b929c;margin-top:0.6em"}
Enforced **structurally**, not by prompting. The tool dispatcher is handed a
read-only `PortfolioReader`, not a connection —
:::

::: {.pull style="font-size:0.92em;border-left-color:#2f7d6e;margin-top:0.4em"}
it cannot write, because it holds no object capable of writing.
:::

::: {.stages style="margin-top:0.5em"}
::: {.stage}
[C2]{.n}[Tool loop runs read-only, **≤ 6 turns** [services/chat.py · run_turn&#40;&#41;]{.m}]{.t}
:::
::: {.stage}
[C3]{.n}[Proposal parked in memory, **expires in 5 min** [services/pending.py]{.m}]{.t}
:::
::: {.stage}
[C4]{.n}[Confirm is **single-use** — a replay is a 410 [routers/chat.py · POST /api/chat/confirm]{.m}]{.t}
:::
:::

::: {style="font-size:0.4em;color:#8b929c;margin-top:0.5em"}
A test runs every tool and asserts the ledger is **byte-for-byte unchanged**.
:::
:::


::: {style="font-size:0.4em;color:#8b929c;margin-top:1em;max-width:15em;line-height:1.5"}
Not distrust of the model. *"Sell everything,"* typed at 2am, should meet a
confirmation dialog like any other destructive action.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
The capability argument is the one worth stealing. Not "we told the model not
to write" — the object graph makes writing unrepresentable.
:::

## Degrade honestly, never guess {.center}

[Figure · value over time, reconstructed from the log]{.kicker}

```{python}
#| label: value-over-time

days  = pd.date_range("2025-07-01", "2026-09-05", freq="B")
n     = len(days)

# Cost basis: a step function that moves only when a transaction is recorded.
buys = {0: 12000, 46: 5200, 120: 7400, 205: 4100, 268: 6300}
cost = np.zeros(n)
running = 0.0
for i in range(n):
    running += buys.get(i, 0)
    cost[i] = running

# Market value: the basis, plus a return path that drifts and drawdowns.
shock = np.zeros(n)
shock[150:185] = np.linspace(0, -0.16, 35)
shock[185:230] = -0.16 + np.linspace(0, 0.19, 45)
ret   = np.cumsum(rng.normal(0.00075, 0.0092, n)) + shock
value = cost * (1 + ret)

# The point of the slide: an unpriceable window is a gap, never a zero.
GAP0, GAP1 = 243, 254
value_gapped = value.copy()
value_gapped[GAP0:GAP1] = np.nan

fig = go.Figure()
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=days, y=cost, mode="lines", name="cost basis",
    line=dict(color=MUTED, width=1.6, shape="hv", dash="dot"),
    hovertemplate="cost basis $%{y:,.0f}<extra></extra>",
))
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=days, y=value_gapped, mode="lines", name="market value",
    line=dict(color=BRASS, width=2.4), connectgaps=False,
    fill="tozeroy", fillcolor="rgba(201,162,39,0.10)",
    hovertemplate="value $%{y:,.0f}<extra></extra>",
))

fig.add_vrect(
    x0=days[GAP0], x1=days[GAP1 - 1],
    fillcolor="rgba(168,68,47,0.20)", line_width=0, layer="below",
)
# Label the band by hand: add_vrect's own annotation anchors to the band edge
# and runs off the right of the plot.
fig.add_annotation(
    x=days[(GAP0 + GAP1) // 2], y=1.0, yref="paper",
    xanchor="right", yanchor="bottom", showarrow=False,
    text="provider down — symbols named, value null",
    font=dict(family="IBM Plex Mono, monospace", size=13, color=LOSS),
)

fig.update_layout(
    height=515, autosize=True,
    yaxis=dict(title="", tickprefix="$", separatethousands=True),
    xaxis=dict(
        rangeslider=dict(visible=False),
        rangeselector=dict(
            buttons=[
                dict(count=1,  label="1M", step="month", stepmode="backward"),
                dict(count=3,  label="3M", step="month", stepmode="backward"),
                dict(count=6,  label="6M", step="month", stepmode="backward"),
                dict(count=1,  label="1Y", step="year",  stepmode="backward"),
                dict(label="ALL", step="all"),
            ],
            bgcolor=SLATE, activecolor=BRASS, bordercolor=GRID, borderwidth=1,
            font=dict(family="IBM Plex Mono, monospace", size=12, color=INK),
            x=0, y=1.12,
        ),
    ),
)
show(fig)
```

::: {.cols}
::: {}
[Illustrative series. Replayed forwards from the whole transaction log, valuing holdings at each day's close — `services/performance.py`.]{.caption}
:::
::: {}
[**The gap is the feature.** A price that is unavailable renders as an em dash, not a zero. A symbol with no history is named, never zero-filled.]{.caption}
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Range buttons mirror the app's own. The red band is a dead provider: the line
stops rather than dropping to zero, because a zero would be a lie that looks
like a crash.
:::

## Four rented services

[What each is for — and what happens without it]{.kicker}

::: {.cols style="margin-top:0.5em"}
::: {.card .fragment}
[Free tier]{.tag}[Finnhub — the price feed]{.h4}

Live prices and symbol search over one permanently open connection. **The only free service offering genuinely real-time US prices over a push connection.**

[**Without it** — no live prices. Cost basis and realized P/L are unaffected: they come from your own ledger.]{.without}
:::

::: {.card .fragment}
[800 req/day]{.tag}[Twelve Data — the history]{.h4}

Daily closes behind both charts. Exists purely to fill Finnhub's gap: history is a paid feature there, discovered only after deploying.

[**Without it** — both charts return a 502 that names the fix. Everything else is unaffected.]{.without}
:::
:::

::: {.cols style="margin-top:0.6em"}
::: {.card .fragment}
[Pay per use]{.tag}[Anthropic — the analyst]{.h4}

Reads holdings, checks prices, reads history, searches the web, answers in plain language. **Proposes; never writes.**

[**Without it** — the chat panel returns 503. The dashboard works normally.]{.without}
:::

::: {.card .fragment}
[~$3 / month]{.tag}[Fly.io — where it runs]{.h4}

One always-on machine, public HTTPS, and a volume that survives restarts. **Hosts that sleep would kill the market socket every time you looked away.**

[**Without it** — the app runs on a laptop, reachable only by you, only while it is awake.]{.without}
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
The "without it" line is the honest part of a dependency slide. Three of the
four degrade to a named error; only Fly is load-bearing, and that is hosting,
not a component.
:::

## Five constraints

[Decisions that shaped everything else]{.kicker}

::: {.stages}
::: {.stage}
[01]{.n}[**Exactly one machine — for correctness, not cost.** [Two copies would open two sockets to a feed that allows one, and double-mount a volume that cannot be. The config pins it explicitly rather than relying on a default.]{.m}]{.t}
:::
::: {.stage}
[02]{.n}[**The transaction log is the only source of truth.** [Holdings, average cost and P/L are recomputed every time. There is deliberately no stored share count.]{.m}]{.t}
:::
::: {.stage}
[03]{.n}[**The model proposes; the person disposes.** [The dispatcher receives a narrow read-only reader, never a connection.]{.m}]{.t}
:::
::: {.stage}
[04]{.n}[**It reports; it never advises.** [No recommendations, price targets or predictions. Asked whether to sell, it declines and offers data.]{.m}]{.t}
:::
::: {.stage}
[05]{.n}[**Degrade honestly, never guess.** [Unavailable prices render as an em dash. Stale quotes are labelled with their age. A dead provider names the symbols it could not price.]{.m}]{.t}
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
If you remember one line from this deck, make it 02. Everything structural
downstream — the FIFO engine, the replay, the refusal to cache positions —
is a consequence of it.
:::

## Figure 3 · How it was built {.center}

[A spec-driven loop with four feedback channels]{.kicker}

```{mermaid}
%%{init: {'theme':'base',
  'fontFamily':'Instrument Sans, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif',
  'flowchart':{'htmlLabels':true,'useMaxWidth':true,'curve':'basis','nodeSpacing':22,'rankSpacing':32},
  'themeVariables':{
  'background':'#0e1116','primaryColor':'#1a2028','primaryTextColor':'#f5f2ec',
  'primaryBorderColor':'#232a33','lineColor':'#5c6672','fontSize':'13px',
  'clusterBkg':'rgba(26,32,40,0.3)','clusterBorder':'#2b3441',
  'edgeLabelBackground':'#0e1116'}}}%%
flowchart LR
  subgraph SPEC["AUTHORED BEFORE THE CODE"]
    direction TB
    P1["plan.md<br/>§1–§14 spec"]
    P2["prompts.md<br/>per-phase asks"]
    P3["CLAUDE.md<br/>durable decisions"]
  end

  S1["1 · Read the<br/>phase spec"]
  S2["2 · Inspect repo<br/>verify externals"]
  S3["3 · Implement<br/>backend · frontend · tests"]
  S4["4 · Verify locally<br/>291 pytest · ruff · tsc"]
  G{"All<br/>green?"}
  S5["5 · Ship<br/>Actions → flyctl"]
  S6["6 · Observe in production<br/>live feed · real market hours"]

  SPEC --> S1 --> S2 --> S3 --> S4 --> G
  G -. "no" .-> S3
  G -->|"yes"| S5 --> S6
  S6 -. "next phase" .-> S1

  classDef spec fill:#151a21,stroke:#3a424c,color:#8b929c
  classDef step fill:#1a2028,stroke:#39424e,color:#f5f2ec
  classDef gate fill:#2a2415,stroke:#c9a227,stroke-width:2.5px,color:#f5f2ec
  class P1,P2,P3 spec
  class S1,S2,S3,S4,S5,S6 step
  class G gate
```

::: {style="font-size:0.46em;line-height:1.55;color:#8b929c;max-width:44em;margin-top:0.5em"}
Written by an AI agent — Claude Code, running Claude Opus 5 — against a
specification authored **before any code existed**. There is no autonomous
task-runner here: each phase was a deliberate, human-initiated cycle.
`CLAUDE.md` is read before each phase and **written back when a decision changes**.
:::

::: {.notes}
Six steps, one gate, two loops back. The spec was written first and is still
the thing each phase is read from.
:::

## How defects surfaced

[Four channels — three of which only fire after deploy]{.kicker}

::: {.stat-grid .cols-4}
::: {.stat .fragment}
[Channel 1]{.label}[Test suite]{.value}[At stage 4, before anything ships. Catches what can be checked in isolation.]{.note}
:::
::: {.stat .fragment}
[Channel 2]{.label}[Code review]{.value}[Found an unbounded cache that every one of the 291 tests passed.]{.note}
:::
::: {.stat .fragment}
[Channel 3]{.label}[Production]{.value}[A status update written but never called — invisible until a real market opened.]{.note}
:::
::: {.stat .fragment}
[Channel 4]{.label}[Screenshots]{.value}[The real browser. A chart dying on a CSS colour token.]{.note}
:::
:::

::: {.pull style="margin-top:1.1em"}
Three of the four only fire after deploy.
:::

::: {style="font-size:0.44em;line-height:1.5;color:#8b929c;margin-top:0.6em;max-width:40em"}
Each produced a fix commit, and the git history **interleaves them with the
phase commits** rather than hiding them.
:::

::: {.notes}
This is the slide that justifies calling it a loop rather than a pipeline. A
test suite alone would have caught exactly one of these four.
:::

## Operations {.center}

[What it costs, and what keeps it alive]{.kicker}

::: {.split}
::: {}
```{python}
#| label: cost-breakdown

items = ["Fly.io machine", "Anthropic", "Fly.io volume", "Twelve Data", "Finnhub"]
mid   = [3.00, 3.00, 0.15, 0.0, 0.0]   # machine is $2–4; chat is per-message
what  = ["Always-on server, public address, HTTPS",
         "Chat, billed per message",
         "1 GB disk the ledger survives on",
         "Price history, 800 requests/day",
         "Live prices, 60 requests/min"]

colours = [BRASS if v > 0 else GAIN for v in mid]

fig = go.Figure(go.Bar(
    x=mid, y=items, orientation="h",
    marker=dict(color=colours, line=dict(color=PAPER, width=1)),
    customdata=what,
    hovertemplate="<b>%{y}</b><br>%{customdata}<br>$%{x:.2f}/mo<extra></extra>",
    text=["  $2–4", "  a few $", "  $0.15", "  free", "  free"],
    textposition="outside", cliponaxis=False,
    textfont=dict(family="IBM Plex Mono, monospace", size=15, color=INK),
))

fig.update_layout(
    height=410, autosize=True, bargap=0.42, showlegend=False,
    xaxis=dict(title="per month", tickprefix="$", range=[0, 6]),
    yaxis=dict(autorange="reversed",
               tickfont=dict(family="IBM Plex Mono, monospace", size=14, color=INK)),
    margin=dict(l=160, r=90, t=20, b=52),
)
show(fig)
```

[Typical total: **under $10/month.** Machine and volume are real prices; the Anthropic line is per-message and depends on use.]{.caption}
:::

::: {}
::: {.card}
[Boot]{.tag}[Migrations run at boot, idempotently]{.h4}

Never as a release command — **that machine runs with no volume attached**, and the work would vanish.
:::

::: {.card style="margin-top:0.7em"}
[Nightly]{.tag}[Snapshot via SQLite online backup]{.h4}

Not a file copy. With write-ahead logging, copying the database without its journal yields a **torn file that looks fine until you need it**.
:::

::: {.card style="margin-top:0.7em"}
[Always]{.tag}[Deploy on every push]{.h4}

GitHub Actions → flyctl. Structured JSON logs.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Two operational details that are easy to get wrong and expensive to discover:
migrations at boot rather than as a release step, and online backup rather than
`cp`. Both are WAL consequences.
:::

## Not investment advice {.center}

::: {style="max-width:24em"}
::: {.pull}
This system reports data and answers questions about it.
:::

::: {style="font-size:0.55em;line-height:1.6;color:#8b929c;margin-top:0.9em"}
Prices may be delayed. Nothing in it is a recommendation to buy or sell
anything — and it is built so that **it cannot become one**.
:::
